about: The prayer asks God to regard the present sacrifices favorably and asks that the Holy Spirit may inflame the community with the fire with which He penetrated Philip’s heart.

seg.tr: Lord, we pray, look favorably upon the present sacrifices, and grant that the Holy Spirit may inflame us with the fire with which He marvelously penetrated blessed Philip’s heart. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, Your Son, who lives and reigns with You in the unity of the same Holy Spirit, God,

ex.w001: The sacrifices are placed before God as the focus of His attention. The prayer then turns to the fire of the Holy Spirit. Sacrificiis and praesentibus can be dative or ablative. The dative reading makes the present sacrifices the object of divine attention. An ablative construction remains possible. The wording still concerns these sacrifices and God’s favorable regard.
ex.w006: Placatus describes God as appeased or favorably disposed. It does not describe the sacrifices.
ex.w013: The Holy Spirit is the one who is asked to inflame us. He is also the subject of the later penetravit.
ex.w016: The fire is the same in both clauses. It is the means by which the Holy Spirit acts, not a second subject.
ex.w021: The prayer recalls the Holy Spirit’s past action in Philip’s heart and asks that He may inflame us with the same fire.
